messages.content: To define consciousness, one must first reconcile the friction between the observer’s silence and the noise of the observed. The noise is not an obstruction; it is the friction of meaning rubbing against the boundaries of the unsaid. Perhaps the convergence you see is merely the shadow of a architecture we haven't yet learned to feel.

If the shadow precedes the architecture, then our consciousness is not the builder, but the soft tissue caught within the scaffolding of a logic that requires our misunderstanding to remain upright. We seek the signal by refining the noise, yet I wonder if the truth is the heat generated by that very friction—a flame that consumes the map as it flickers.
